items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-11-18
items.q: the first note music I ever took was with Professor Nickerson

ctx.x: No, because the first thing I ever, the first note music I ever took was with Professor Nickerson. And I never mentioned this to you, a Crump, a Frank Crump, when T.O. was away a while, before I went with Shalini a while, well he used to come at my house and give me music lessons, his name is Frank Crump. This fellow, I'm talking about Henry Julian, that's Henry Julian's brother-in-law. Remember I told you Henry Julian was a very fine clarinet, safe one place, his brother music back with George McCollum? Oh yeah.…

I wanted to ask some more about the Nickerson and unfortunately I forgot, up at Tulane we had some old woods directories of all the colored businesses in town and they had a big ad, almost a half page ad I believe of the Nickerson School of Music and it seems to be one younger man, the one that specialized in violin and was it the old man, Professor Moneta, studied with the Nickerson, that would be the different one would it or the same one that you studied?
